hypothesis.title: Latent Score Identity
hypothesis.question: Can a fixed foreground musical loop acquire clearer identity when redundant low-salience modulation, voicing, and spectral marks are composed as a latent score?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If one identical foreground loop is rendered with a coordinated latent score of low-frequency modulation profiles, recurrent voicing fingerprints, and subtle spectral-bin/phase gestures, then blinded listeners will report stronger identity and continuity than in a foreground-only control, because identity-relevant information can be carried redundantly in time-frequency, rhythmic, and pitch-content layers without changing the named melody or harmony.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: APC watermarking shows that robust information can be embedded across STFT phase and adjacent log-magnitude structure while preserving perceptual quality [S1]. Basso continuo style identification shows that performer identity can live in pitch-content realization choices inside a rule-governed harmonic practice [S2]. Rhythm formant analysis shows that low-frequency amplitude modulation captures macro-temporal identity-bearing structure complementary to spectral features [S3]. MSU-Bench frames score understanding as multilevel rather than single-channel [S5], while Tonnetz/combinatorial geometry provides a formal model for latent harmonic adjacency [S6]. Falsification criterion: if blinded ratings show no reliable difference in identity, continuity, or performer-like character between the latent-score render and the foreground-only control, the hypothesis is not supported.

recipe.title: Latent Score Identity Micro-Study
recipe.bodyMd:
## Goal
Compare whether a foreground-identical loop gains recognizable identity from a composed latent score.

## Shared Arrangement
- Length: 60 seconds.
- Tempo: 96 BPM.
- Meter: 4/4.
- Harmony: one eight-bar loop repeated with identical melody, bass, chord roots, instrumentation, mix balance, and loudness across versions.

## Versions
- Version A: foreground-only control. No deliberate latent profile beyond normal production.
- Version B: rhythm-formant latent score. Shape section-level amplitude modulation profiles in the 1-10 Hz range: stable pulse, dispersed pulse, clustered pulse, then mixed pulse [S3].
- Version C: spectral/voicing latent score. Keep foreground fixed but add recurrent voicing fingerprints inspired by griffs [S2], Tonnetz-adjacent inner-voice moves [S6], and very subtle phase/noise-band gestures distributed across the phrase [S1].

## Evaluation
Blind-label A/B/C. Rate each for identity clarity, continuity, and whether it feels like the same performer/system returning. Note any bars where the latent layer becomes too obvious or distracts from the foreground. Evidence basis: [S1, S2, S3, S5, S6].

parameters.value: identity clarity / continuity / performer-like character ratings

dawChecklist: Create one 60-second loop at 96 BPM and freeze melody, harmony, instruments, effects, and mix balance.
Render Version A with no deliberate latent modulation profile.
For Version B, automate amplitude envelopes or sidechain patterns to create four distinct low-frequency modulation profiles while preserving notes and chords.
For Version C, add recurring inner-voice voicing fingerprints, subtle Tonnetz-adjacent movements, and low-level spectral/phase/noise gestures distributed across the phrase.
Blind-label the files and rate identity clarity, continuity, and performer-like character.
Mark any moments where the latent layer becomes foreground distraction.
Compare whether Version B or C produces stronger identity without changing the named musical objects.

protocol.listeningContext: Quiet room; repeat once on headphones and once on monitors at fixed playback level.
protocol.listeningMethod: Blinded three-arm comparison with 1-7 ratings and bar-level notes.
whatVaries: presence and type of latent score: none vs low-frequency modulation vs spectral/voicing marks
